Hi! I'm a 2nd-year B.Tech AI & ML student passionate about innovation, technology, and solving real-world problems.

I'm working on EARTH PULSE, an intelligent Earth monitoring platform using NASA satellite data, AI/ML, and interactive visualizations to track climate change, deforestation, water resources, and environmental changes.

I have interests in Python, AI/ML, web development, and research, along with hackathon experience (3rd place, Manthan4Yuva 2026).
summary:
Earth Pulse is an interactive Earth System Trend Investigation platform developed to make NASA Earth science data easier to explore and understand.

Our application uses the NASA POWER Monthly Point API, providing historical environmental data based on NASA's MERRA-2 reanalysis. Users can investigate four environmental variables: temperature, precipitation, relative humidity, and wind speed across selected locations and time periods.

To address NASA's Earth System Trend Detective challenge, Earth Pulse processes historical data, visualizes time-series patterns, compares locations, and applies statistical methods such as the Modified Mann-Kendall test and Sen's slope to identify trend direction, rate of change, and statistical significance.

Built using Streamlit, Python, Pandas, NumPy, SciPy, and Plotly, the platform presents complex scientific information through interactive graphs and an accessible interface.

Earth Pulse helps students, researchers, and the public investigate environmental changes with greater clarity and transparency. Its goal is to turn complex Earth science data into understandable scientific insights, supporting informed exploration rather than weather prediction.
details:
Earth Pulse – Making Earth Science Understandable

Earth Pulse is an interactive, location-based Earth System Trend Investigation platform designed to make NASA Earth science data easier to explore and understand.

Users can select a city or enter geographical coordinates, choose an environmental variable, and investigate historical changes over a selected time period.

Our application retrieves monthly environmental data through the NASA POWER Monthly Point API. Currently, it supports four variables:

  • Temperature (T2M)
  • Relative Humidity (RH2M)
  • Precipitation (PRECTOTCORR)
  • Wind Speed (WS10M)

The application processes the retrieved data using Python, Pandas, and NumPy. It applies the Hamed–Rao Modified Mann–Kendall test to examine statistical significance and Sen's Slope to estimate the rate of change. Users can explore interactive graphs, compare two geographical locations, examine data coverage, and download investigation reports.

The platform is built using Streamlit, Python, SciPy, Plotly, and Requests. An interactive 3D Earth globe is developed using JavaScript, HTML, CSS, and Three.js.

Our creative approach combines location-based exploration, beginner-friendly explanations, bilingual interface elements, and transparent statistical analysis in one platform.

Earth Pulse is designed for students, educators, researchers, and the public. Our goal is to help people understand what is changing, where it is changing, and how much it is changing.

We also considered scientific accuracy, missing data, data sources, uncertainty, accessibility, and the limitations of environmental datasets. Earth Pulse investigates historical environmental trends; it does not claim to predict daily weather or establish the causes of environmental changes.
